title: Sox's Lane: starting out with Eddie Vincent and a four-piece band
summary: Tom recalls Sox's Lane as where he began playing, forming a four-piece band with Eddie Vincent, Skeeter and Jolie on bass.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: That's right. I see. I wanted to ask you something else too. All the different places you live. And they all jazzed when you grew up? What's the name of that place? Well… From that lane over there? Sox's Lane. Sox's?

Yeah. Joan Sox Lane. Oh, that was a man's name. No, I don't know what the man's name was. I know that's the name. They called it Joan Sox. Joan Sox Lane. Yeah. Well, that's the first place I started to play. Me, Eddie Vincent. Mm-hmm. You never told you, heard about Eddie Vincent?
I heard him on records. Yeah. With Freddie Kepler.

With Freddie Kepler. That's right. Mm-hmm. Well, I was the one who pitched him. Mm-hmm. Yeah. Me and him just started together in Sox's Lane. Mm-hmm. That's been years ago. Mm-hmm. And then we made up a band with Skeeter. Like you see, it was Skeeter and different fellas. And I coached him playing all around. And then I started to take a lesson with the violin. You understand? I was playing to get all my cymbals. I didn't play in the band without him. Mm-hmm. After I started taking lessons, I got to divide and I started reading. Mm-hmm. Yeah. We had a four-piece band, you see. Skeeter. Skeeter. Eddie Vincent. Me. And the fella called Play Bass. And what is his name? What is it? Peter. Peter. Peter something. He used to play bass with us. Yeah. And nobody had a fella named that called Joe-Joe. Churniel. He was way down the Lee's Lane. So he called him Churniel. He used to play bass with us. Yes, call him Jolie.
Is that about where McClellanville is?
Yeah, McClellanville, down there McClellanville. That's right. You could have been all around you, eh? Yeah. Why you ain't been?
